newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher lifts stake in Kupe Gas.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher lifts stake in Kupe Gas.

text.p: Fletcher Energy Ltd said on Wednesday it had lifted its stake in the Kupe gas field to 36.75 percent from 2.5 percent and simultaneously bought and onsold a 25.75 percent stake to state power generator Electricity Corp of New Zealand.
Chief Executive Michael Andrews said: "The increase in our interest in the Kupe field is a further significant step in our development as an oil and gas operator.
"With our partners in the Kupe Joint Venture, we will be taking appropriate steps to develop the resource."

The acquisition of the additional Kupe participation will add approximately 20 million barrels of oil equivalent of proven and probable reserves, at an effective finding cost of US$0.90 per barrel, Andrews said.
Decisions on the development programme would be made and announced in due course by the Kupe Joint Venture, he added.

ECNZ said in a statement that the acquisition of a significant interest in Kupe complemented its aim of maintaining long-termal thermal generation capacity. ECNZ generates electricity from gas and coal at its 1,000 megawatt Huntly power station near Hamilton in the North Island.
